t: Strengths for the Persian army run from 14,000 or 15,000 in one modern estimate to Arrian's almost 20,000 infantry and 20,000 cavalry, and Justin's 600,000 is judged fantastical.
The ancient accounts disagree about how the battle began: Arrian and Plutarch describe an assault across a defended river, Diodorus a crossing at dawn that met no resistance.
The Persian army was not destroyed, and many of its men retreated to Halicarnassus, but Sardis fell and Alexander marched on to Halicarnassus without significant obstacles.
dyk: Before the battle some Macedonian officers objected that custom forbade fighting in the month of Daisios, and Alexander is said to have solved this by declaring the month a second Artemision.
ev: Philip II wins at Chaeronea and forms the Hellenic League to make war on Persia, while Artaxerxes III is murdered
A Macedonian expeditionary corps lands in Asia Minor, Philip is murdered and Alexander III and Darius III take their thrones
Memnon of Rhodes defeats a Macedonian force and most Greek cities return to Persian control
Alexander marches to the Hellespont and crosses into Asia Minor
Alexander defeats the Persian satraps' army at the Granicus
Dascylium, Sardis and Ephesus fall to Alexander or are evacuated by their garrisons
Alexander besieges Miletus, which resists him

f.date: May 334 BCE, in the Macedonian month of Daisios
f.place: The crossing of the Granicus (now the Biga River) in the Troad, on the road from Abydus to Dascylium, in north-western Turkey; the exact ford is debated
f.sides: Macedon under Alexander III, with 12,000 heavy infantry, 1,000 light infantry and 5,100 cavalry, 18,100 men in all; the Persian satraps of Asia Minor, with Arsites probably in overall command, and Memnon of Rhodes, with strengths that range from 14,000 or 15,000 in one modern estimate to almost 20,000 infantry and 20,000 cavalry in Arrian
f.outcome: Alexander defeated the Persian field army and the Greek mercenaries behind it. The Persians were forced onto the defensive in the cities they still held in the region.
